review_note: A torsor under any sheaf of possibly noncommutative groups is trivial precisely when it has a global section. Checked prepared statement against its pinned original-source theorem excerpt in Stage A; source proofs/remarks not opened. Non-authoritative preliminary verdict.
statement:
A $\mathcal G$-torsor on a site $\mathcal C$ means a sheaf of sets $\mathcal F$ with a left action of a sheaf of groups $\mathcal G$, simply transitive on sections whenever these are nonempty, and locally admitting a section after a covering of every object. The trivial torsor is $\mathcal G$ acting on itself by left multiplication. Here $\Gamma(\mathcal C,\mathcal F)$ is the set of global sections (natural transformations from the final sheaf to $\mathcal F$).

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a sheaf of (possibly non-commutative)
groups on $\mathcal{C}$.
A $\mathcal{G}$-torsor $\mathcal{F}$ is trivial if and only if
$\Gamma(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{F}) \not = \emptyset$.
hypotheses: $\mathcal C$ is a site; $\mathcal G$ is a sheaf of groups (not necessarily commutative) on it.
$\mathcal F$ is a $\mathcal G$-torsor as defined in sites-cohomology.tex:241–272.
conclusions: $\mathcal F$ is isomorphic to the trivial $\mathcal G$-torsor if and only if $\Gamma(\mathcal C,\mathcal F)$ is nonempty.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-trivial-torsor}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a sheaf of (possibly non-commutative)
groups on $\mathcal{C}$.
A $\mathcal{G}$-torsor $\mathcal{F}$ is trivial if and only if
$\Gamma(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{F}) \not = \emptyset$.

review_note: Degree-one cohomology of an abelian sheaf canonically classifies its torsors up to isomorphism. Checked prepared statement against its pinned original-source theorem excerpt in Stage A; source proofs/remarks not opened. Non-authoritative preliminary verdict.
statement:
A torsor for an abelian sheaf $\mathcal H$ on a site $\mathcal C$ is a sheaf of sets with a locally nonempty, simply transitive $\mathcal H$-action. The group $H^1(\mathcal C,\mathcal H)$ is the first right-derived functor of global sections in the abelian category of abelian sheaves on $\mathcal C$.

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Let $\mathcal{H}$ be an abelian sheaf on $\mathcal{C}$.
There is a canonical bijection between the set of isomorphism
classes of $\mathcal{H}$-torsors and $H^1(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{H})$.
hypotheses: $\mathcal H$ is an abelian sheaf on $\mathcal C$.
conclusions: The set of isomorphism classes of $\mathcal H$-torsors is canonically in bijection with $H^1(\mathcal C,\mathcal H)$.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-torsors-h1}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Let $\mathcal{H}$ be an abelian sheaf on $\mathcal{C}$.
There is a canonical bijection between the set of isomorphism
classes of $\mathcal{H}$-torsors and $H^1(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{H})$.
